claim: FIRST per-node LLM router run with engine hook live (ab47e9220) on nomad2018: the router DID diverge per-node — startup decision was sonnet-all (matching E003 family default), but the async per-node decision for node_1 was haiku-all (cross-the-board downgrade for shallow exploration). The mechanism works. HOWEVER haiku-coder produced train.py with `import yaml`, yaml not in env, training crashed, no further nodes attempted (selector_round_2 evidently didn't propose new nodes after node_1 failure or other crashes), aggregator refused to ensemble nothing, pipeline failed with no submission. Total $3.82 burned, no medal. This validates the routing infrastructure but exposes a real LLM-router failure mode: aggressive cross-role haiku downgrade without env-awareness lets haiku coder write code with non-installed deps. The router prompt needs an 'environment guarantee' constraint OR per-node routing should not downgrade coder below a floor.

router_decisions.matches: no — DIVERGED from startup decision and family default
router_decisions.interpretation: router downgraded for shallow exploration (depth=1, no parent_metric yet); consistent with P1 cost-protection but too aggressive: coder also went haiku

failure_mode.consequence: trainer exited 1 → node 1 status=failed → no metric → no other nodes succeeded → aggregator refused to ensemble nothing → Pipeline failed
failure_mode.root_cause_hypothesis: haiku-coder, lacking the rigor of sonnet/opus, wrote a train.py that imported yaml without checking availability. Sonnet/opus typically inspect the env or use json/pickle. The LLM router did not warn the coder of env constraints because the routing-policy prompt and the per-node context do not carry env info.

scope: Single run. Validates the M2-followup engine hook (per-node decisions are recorded and applied) and exposes a real LLM-router-prompt-design issue.
limitations: Cannot tell if the failure was bad luck (haiku ALWAYS uses yaml here?) or a systematic haiku-coder pattern. A rerun with sonnet-on-coder pinned would isolate the env issue from the routing logic.
Did not inspect the router_cache for the prompt/reasoning the LLM emitted (the router_cache lives at memory/routing/router_cache/calls/<task>/...).
confidence: medium-high (the divergence mechanism is confirmed; the failure-mode attribution is plausible but n=1)

implications.design_finding_for_per_node_router: Cross-the-board haiku downgrade on shallow nodes is dangerous because haiku-coder may write code with unverified deps. Mitigation candidates: (a) add an 'env constraint' line to routing_policy.md so the LLM router avoids haiku-coder for unfamiliar tasks; (b) introduce a coder-floor static rule in policy.json § per_node (coder >= sonnet); (c) feed an env-fingerprint into NodeRoutingContext so the router has signal.
implications.follow_up: E-PN4-nomad-rerun-with-coder-floor: same task, router_strategy=llm + per_node_routing=true, BUT add a static coder-floor rule (coder cannot go below sonnet). Expect: valid submission, medal=gold ($16 ish), confirming the failure was the haiku-coder, not the routing logic.

next_actions: Design experiment 2: E-PN4-nomad-rerun (coder pinned to sonnet via models_by_role override, per_node_routing still on for the other 8 roles).
If experiment 2 succeeds → write E029 confirming the haiku-coder hypothesis, propose a coder-floor rule for the per_node static block.
